title: Chapter 166: Isn't She Dead?
html:
Examining the bags more closely, Chen Ge’s expression darkened. He rubbed a fingertip over the names and found the problem: the ink on several was still wet. Someone had labeled them only moments ago.

His head snapped up. The nurses’ station contained nowhere to hide.

“Whoever dispensed these pills must still be nearby.” He did not know whether they had noticed him, but caution was essential. Vaulting over the counter, he slipped into the room opposite and watched the corridor through a narrow crack in the door.

“Fresh labels mean the prescriptions were just prepared. Who dispenses medicine here at midnight?” Several possibilities occurred to him, foremost among them the twisted-faced man. A former doctor with a deep hunger for revenge, he seemed the likeliest candidate.

“Does he drug his victims by force?” But if so, carefully writing a name on every bag served no purpose. The answer was more complicated. Midnight made the hospital especially unstable, yet Chen Ge decided to wait until he understood the medicine.

Ten minutes later, a blurred silhouette appeared at the corridor’s far end. From that distance, he could not tell whether it emerged from a room or another floor.

“Which patient is that?” He could not see its face and dared not use the flashlight. Hammer ready, he remained behind the door. The shadow staggered forward with an unnatural gait, perpetually on the verge of falling.

As it drew nearer, he noticed something stranger still: its steps made no sound.

“With a limp like that, silence should be impossible.”

Soon he could distinguish its clothing. A white nurse’s uniform stood out sharply against the dark corridor and its filthy mattresses.

“Not the twisted-faced man—a woman?” Still uncertain, Chen Ge leaned against the door and fixed one unblinking eye on the gap. “She’s coming.”

Head lowered, the uniformed shadow mumbled to itself. Only when it neared his room did he see it clearly.

A monster wore the nurse’s coat. Its waist was broken, its limbs wrenched into impossible angles, as though someone had dismantled a body and reassembled it incorrectly. The sight destroyed every comforting association Chen Ge had ever held with nurses. Behind the door, sweat slicked his grip on the hammer.

Tangled black hair concealed most of her face. As she passed his hiding place, she suddenly stopped. Chen Ge held his breath and raised the hammer.

The dead nurse seemed to sense him. Slowly, she lifted her head, and the hair parted around a familiar face.

It’s her!Nothing about the face itself was extraordinary, but recognition shocked him. Her black-and-white portrait hung in the second sick hall’s auditorium.

But she’s dead.This was the nurse murdered in the Third Sick Hall. Doctor Gao had said the police believed one of the patients killed her.

She still wanders the halls?That explained the silent footsteps. His hand moved toward the cleaver. After a moment’s hesitation, the nurse laboriously turned, then let her broad body topple toward the door concealing him.

DONG!

Her skull struck the door with a dull thud. Chen Ge jumped back and drew the cleaver. The door had no lock; if she entered, he was prepared to fight.

Then another door opened downstairs. At the sound, the nurse turned like a puppet jerked by invisible strings. She crossed to the nurses’ station and entered the small room beside it.

What was that?Sweat drenched Chen Ge’s back. The nurse was probably among the weakest entities in the Third Sick Hall, a mindless lingering spirit following someone else’s commands. Her master was the true danger.

He kept his guard raised but remained hidden, unwilling to startle her by charging out with the cleaver.

Inside the nurses’ station, she retrieved a thick notebook stained with dirt and blood, consulted its pages, and began sorting the bags of medication.

From the room opposite, Chen Ge saw everything. Her hands moved with practiced speed. Soon she gathered about ten bags and shuffled into the stairwell toward the fourth floor.

Once she disappeared, Chen Ge crossed to the station and examined the notebook. Its thick pages contained patient files and diagnostic reports.

Leafing through them, he discovered that every listed patient was dead. On each report, someone had crossed out the original diagnosis in red and written: Confirmed Dead.

Have the killers hiding inside this hospital been following the patients? Or have the patients who once received treatment here returned to this place?

Lee Chunyan and Zhang Qisi appeared in the notebook. The medication bags bearing those names were now gone.

Their names are written on dolls upstairs. Every deceased patient seems to have a corresponding doll in the Third Sick Hall, and each night a “person” gives them medicine as if they were still alive.

The hospital had been abandoned for five years, yet the Third Sick Hall continued operating. Only its patients had changed—from the living to the dead. The mysterious door might be responsible for everything.

Has the door remained open so long that the world behind it has begun overlapping reality?

He put the notebook in his backpack without reading further and headed down the corridor. Before the nurse returned, he wanted to inspect the third-floor bathroom.
